title: Progressive error-budget bands, regional reservation & staggered circuit-breaker policy for model routes
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Scope: establish a consistent, implementable pattern for per-model-route SLI definitions, SLO targets, progressive error-budget bands, regional reservation guardrails, and staggered circuit-breaker actions. This ticket produces the policy text, example SLO declarations for a representative set of LLM routes (chat, completion-short, completion-long, embeddings), enforcement thresholds, and an actionable rollout plan with dashboards and runbook entries.

Background: we have fragmented SLOs across teams and routes, and incidents where blunt global circuit breakers caused unnecessary capacity throttling. Multiple customers have requested clearer guarantees and a predictable error-budget consumption model that integrates multi-region failover and Dedicated reservations. This work consolidates learnings from past incidents and proposes a pattern that blends conservative regional reservations with progressive degradation (to preserve high-priority traffic) and staged circuit-breakers to avoid cascade failures.
proposal_summary: Define SLIs (success-rate, p99 latency, model-quality regression) and SLOs expressed as a combination of availability and latency targets per route. Introduce 3 error-budget bands (Green/Amber/Red) tied to operational actions: monitoring alerts, automated throttles & model fallbacks, and finally prioritized shedding with regional failover. Circuit breakers are staggered by priority tier and by region; Dedicated reservations and burst bands are reserved and consumed according to a borrowing policy. Provide concrete policies, example configuration snippets for the routing layer, and dashboard/alert templates.
slis: request_success_rate: fraction of requests returning a 2xx generation response within the timeout window (excludes client cancellations). Primary SLI for availability/quality decisions.
p99_latency_tokenized: 99th percentile server-side tail latency measured in ms, normalized to token-completion time for generation routes.
model_quality_regression: periodic eval pass-rate on canonical prompt set (daily) — fraction of prompts meeting quality threshold for the model variant.
queued_retries: ratio of requests that were retried after temporary throttling and later succeeded within 30s — used to detect harmful retry storms.
error_rate_by_category: SLI buckets for failure classes (infrastructure 5xx, model OOM, model decode errors) to drive targeted mitigations.
slo_definitions: chat.high_priority (route: /v1/chat): availability 99.95% monthly (success_rate), p99_latency < 550ms, model_quality_regression >= 99% on daily smoke set.
note: SLOs are deliberately stricter for embeddings and high-priority chat routes; long completion routes accept higher latency and slightly lower availability due to resource footprint.
error_budget_policy: Define monthly error budget = 1 - SLO_target. Track burn rate over sliding 7d and 30d windows.
Green band (<=20% burn of monthly budget): monitoring only; no traffic controls. Trigger internal 'SLO-approaching' Slack notification when 10% of budget used in 7d window.

Amber band (20%-60% burn): recommended mitigations include: reduce batch sizes for affected model variant, enable prefix KV-cache for cached routes, apply lightweight quantization variant fallback for non-sensitive routes; issue PagerDuty for SRE review if sustained > 12h.

Red band (>60% burn): automated protective actions: enable staggered circuit-breaker stage-1 (rate limit non-critical API keys), stage-2 (fallback to lower-cost/latency model variant for defined routes), stage-3 (regional failover and reservation reallocation). Human-in-loop required before eviction of P0 traffic.
Borrowing policy: short-term borrowing from Dedicated burst pool allowed up to 10% of reservation for 30 minutes with automatic reconciliation; Admin audit log entry required for >60 minutes.
circuit_breaker_policy: Principle: avoid single global kill-switch. Circuit-breakers are tiered: soft (throttle), medium (fallback), hard (reject/evict). Each stage has region and priority awareness.
Soft threshold: sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m at p95 traffic => apply token-bucket throttling to non-critical keys (10-30% reduction).
Medium threshold: sustained p99_latency breach and error-budget in Amber for >30m => route non-P0 traffic to fallback model variant and enforce per-route concurrency caps.

Hard threshold: regional capacity exhaustion + Red error budget => initiate regional circuit-breaker: move traffic to other regions per failover policy and evict non-P0 keys until capacity stabilizes.
Circuit-breaker cooldowns: exponential backoff with manual override. Automated reopen only after health-check SLI window meets Green criteria for 15m.
multi_region_failover: Reservation bands: reserve three bands per region for each priority tier: guaranteed (P0), burst (P1), opportunistic (P2). Guaranteed reservation must be >= 50% of peak P0 demand observed in last 30d for customer-critical deployments.
Failover order: local region -> sibling region within same cloud provider -> cross-provider region (if configured) -> degrade to fallback model variant in original region.

Traffic weighting: use weighted-round-robin with health probes and per-region budget allowances; weights adjusted automatically when a region enters Amber/Red band to keep P0 traffic within guaranteed reservations.

Orchestration: routing control-plane will annotate requests with 'failover-hint' and 'priority' headers for downstream enforcement; changes are staged via canary and gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
load_shedding_strategies: Graceful degrade sequence (highest to lowest cost impact): 1) shorten generation max_tokens for non-P0 requests, 2) prefer cached completions, 3) fall back to distilled/quantized model variant, 4) return syntactic placeholder response with an explicit 'degraded' flag when quality cannot be guaranteed.
Priority-aware shedding: always preserve P0 chat turn completion; shed embeddings and long completions before P0 chat routes.
Adaptive admission controller: use leaky-bucket admission that accounts for token budget and current KV-cache hit rate to decide admit/reject at edge.
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboard: 'SLO Health - Model Routes' with SLI trendlines (success_rate, p99 latency), error budget burn chart, active circuit-breaker state heatmap by region and route.
Example query (PromQL-like): 'sum(rate(generation_errors_total[5m])) by (route,region) / sum(rate(generation_requests_total[5m])) by (route,region)  -> failure ratio'.
Alerting: SLO-warning (20% monthly budget used in 7d) -> email + Slack; SLO-critical (60% monthly budget used in 7d) -> PD escalation + auto-mitigation trigger.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc reviewed and approved by Reliability and Platform PMs (sign-off from Priya Nair and Tomas Becker).
Example SLO declarations for the four representative routes committed to infra-config-repo and validated in staging via synthetic traffic harness.
Dashboards and alerts created in Grafana with links in the ticket and smoke checks passing for 72h in canary rollout.
Automated circuit-breaker stages implemented in routing layer with test harness that simulates Amber/Red band behaviors and verifies correct fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize policy and examples; get PM and SRE review.
Week 1: commit SLO declarations and deploy dashboards/alerts to staging.
Week 2: implement soft throttling logic in routing canary (10% traffic), run chaos tests to force Amber band.
Week 3: enable medium fallback policies in canary, validate synthetic quality regressions and customer-impact matrix.
Week 4: expand to 50% traffic with monitoring; if stable, full rollout and postmortem review.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: automated fallbacks may produce unacceptable quality regressions for some customers. Mitigation: require model-quality_regression checks and enable per-customer opt-out for automatic fallback; add explicit API header for 'no-fallback'.
Risk: rapid cross-region failover can saturate egress links. Mitigation: implement pacing on failover ramp and pre-warm sibling region capacity via burst reservation.
Risk: monitoring blind spots for custom/private deployments. Mitigation: include a short onboarding checklist for Private deployments to ensure SLO telemetry is forwarded to central observability.
